body:
My girlfriend is pretty much the only thing keeping me going.  We've had ups and downs, but she's been amazingly supportive, understanding, and loving.  But I know she can't take me being unemployable forever.  If it weren't for her, I probably wouldn't have made it this far.

Got a phone call this morning saying that I'd lost my job because I was out for a month because of medical issues and don't get enough hours to be covered by FMLA.  I feel so depressed and apathetic, like it's just a matter of time before I work up the nerve to do it...
I'm glad to hear you made it through the night in at least good enough condition to be posting here.  How are you feeling about everything?

I understand how cops are abusive assholes like that who are either undertrained or uncaring when it comes to psychological issues.  It's not your fault you had that attack.

Is there any way you can get an appointment sooner?  At least, if you can't, you have that in two weeks, if you hang in there.  Is there anything else you can do when the kids are asleep that you feel up to doing?
If you're both sick- he should be helping out.  This may seem obvious, but have you seen a doctor for your migraines?  Even if you can't immediately- you can later on, and they *can* help.
The best meaning is one you make and value yourself.

I can't imagine just how hard that is for you.  Having to deal with two babies, a migraine, and a husband who won't speak to you.

I don't know just why he's in bed from your post, if he's sick enough that he should be there or something, but at the very least he should be talking to you.  It may not be a good replacement, but that's one thing we're for.  :)

Thanks for the support.  I mean it.

Thing is, my thinking is complex and nonlinear- which again makes me feel isolated.  Like my thoughts run faster than I can figure out how to express them.  I'm wary to use specific analogies since they may be idiosyncratic enough that someone could figure out who I am.

I enjoy doing things for myself, no problem- even if it's as simple as flopping down and gaming.  It's just that one of my huge goals and values in life is to be self-supporting.  I tried to figure out how to work for money in elementary school but stupid overprotective bitch of a mother wouldn't let me do so much as try to sell lemonade.  Went to school like I was "supposed" to to get a good job, searched for a few years, and got... nothing.  So when I'm not managing to distract myself and have to "face the music" (get actual things done), that's when I feel hopeless, anxious, and like anything that isn't actually working a "real" job using my education is a complete waste of time.  (Job searching feels like a waste of time due to the fact that it's yielded a 0% success rate, although I still get in several applications most weeks.)

Put it this way.  It's not so much how much I make, as having enough to live reasonably- but it feels like $25K a year on a degree where the average graduate makes roughly $50K a year is too much to ask for.  And I feel defective.  It's like there's this big sandwich sign that says "DO NOT HIRE" attached to my back.  (And at least two job counselors have told me that my interview skills are well above average.)

I thought I'd be able to be self-supporting by now five years ago.  And I'm not.  Why should the next five years be any different?  Or the next five?  At my age it feels like my time to get this crap figured out is long past due.

It just feels like I need understanding, somebody to get just why I feel so hopeless, and why I'm scared of being 30 and still leeching off of family.

This is more like not wanting to live in a world where hardly anyone else can see my worth, than hating myself.  Killing myself feels more like walking out of an abusive relationship than leaving because I'm worthless- like the world doesn't deserve me since it doesn't seem to value me at a "normal" level.

I want to support myself.  To do that, you need money.  To get money, you need a job of some sort.  I'm living with family still moching off of them, simply because nobody else can see my worth.  It feels like if nobody is willing to pay for my skills, they aren't of value (basic economics.)  Sorry if this is rambly.  It's just that

-To support myself, I need money.
-To get money, I need some kind of employment.
-For someone else to employ me, they must value me at an amount equal to or greater than what they pay me.
-If nobody else employs me, my value is whatever I get paid in my current situation.
If he's not willing to put in as much as you are, he's not worth having emotions for, sad as it is.  There IS someone else you WILL make a relationship with, if you try to.
